title: Existence of one integration-normalized diagonal chart
statement: For [def-pur-conventions] and a separated finite-type smooth f:X→Y of pure relative dimension d with finite-type structural maps aX,aY and f aY=aX, every finite-type affine target open V has a Chart as defined by [def-pur-diagonal-orientation-refinement-data]. Its normal comparison satisfies BetaNormalized for every vector presentation preserving projection and zero.

proof.text: Apply affineTargetDiagonalDnc to this V. The Rees normal-bundle theorem constructs its rank-d conormal vector presentation with the actual projection and augmentation.
The unit integration adjunct is invertible. Pull it back along zero and compose the Tate isomorphisms; transport its inverse through the specified model section exchange to construct beta.

For a second vector model, compare both by their composite isomorphism over the identity. Zero-section integration base change and section-exchange pasting identify the transported maps, giving BetaNormalized in every model.
